supporting_observations.claim: At 13:40:29 UTC, the proxy logged an HTTP 200 response to a request for https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nwd-it/tools/main/u.ps1 from WS-ICHEN-01, authenticated as NWD\ivy.chen. This is temporally consistent with the reported window appearance.

The script request and its CONNECT setup share tunnel ID PT-b8cd79a6b5f1d97c and client source port 64473. Zeek independently records a connection from the workstation to the explicit proxy on that source port.

A separate simultaneous CONNECT to raw.githubusercontent.com advertises Firefox. It has no shared tunnel ID or source port linking it to the inspected script request, so its browser user-agent cannot establish which process requested u.ps1.

The successful request for a .ps1 resource near the reported time warrants investigation, but these network records establish neither script execution nor its purpose. They do not support either a malicious finding or a benign closure by themselves.

known_telemetry_limitations: No PowerShell process creation, command line, parent process, or script-block content for the reported 13:40 activity is supplied. The relevant proxy and Zeek records provide no initiating PID (T033-00089, T033-00091, T033-00093).
The inspected GET records the URL and HTTP status, but not the response body, script hash, or repository ownership verification (T033-00091).
Proxy authentication as ivy.chen does not identify the person initiating the request or prove that PowerShell made it (T033-00089, T033-00091).
claims_not_established: Whether the reported window executed u.ps1 or was unrelated to its retrieval (T033-00091).
Whether u.ps1 contained malicious code, legitimate maintenance logic, or other content; the nwd-it repository name does not establish organizational authorization (T033-00091).
Whether the alerted activity was the documented IT patching workflow; the available request does not establish execution of the approved internal Apply-Updates.ps1 script (T033-00091).

Whether the alerted activity caused persistence, credential theft, lateral movement, or exfiltration; no causal execution chain is established by the script-request records (T033-00089, T033-00091, T033-00093).
additional_evidence_needed: Collect WS-ICHEN-01 EDR process ancestry, Security 4688, Sysmon process/network events, and PowerShell 4103/4104 logs around 13:40 UTC to identify the process behind source port 64473 and recover its commands.
Recover the exact response body or cached artifact for T033-00091, calculate its hash, and examine the repository revision served at the event time without executing it.
Confirm repository ownership and authorization with IT, and obtain patching execution records from WS-SOKAFOR-01 and the internal script share.
Ask ivy.chen what application, document, link, or command was used immediately before the window appeared; correlate the response with browser history and endpoint artifacts.
unrelated_findings: Separate authentication review: sam.okafor obtained Kerberos tickets from WS-ICHEN-01's address and subsequently had a network logon to WS-SOKAFOR-01 from that address. This is not proof of remote administration or credential compromise and has no established link to the reported window (T033-00014, T033-00015, T033-00017, T033-00019).

Separate authentication review: leo.martins obtained tickets from WS-ICHEN-01's address and had a network logon to WS-NBLAKE-01 from that address at approximately 14:13 UTC. No link to the alerted activity is established (T033-00235, T033-00237, T033-00238, T033-00249).

Separate software-policy ticket: a Dropbox updater ran as SYSTEM on WS-ICHEN-01 at 14:12 UTC. Dropbox is outside the supplied approved cloud-storage inventory; these records do not establish file synchronization or exfiltration (T033-00210, T033-00211).

Separate application review: Webex.exe launched with a Gmail URL argument at 14:15 UTC. The unusual argument has no established relationship to the reported PowerShell activity (T033-00276, T033-00277).
